verdict.rationale: RustDesk documents a free open-source ID/rendezvous server (hbbs) and relay server (hbbr) you deploy on your own infrastructure, with a Docker Compose setup, and clients connect peer to peer or fall back to your relay. Several community users report running their own lookup/relay servers successfully, sometimes for years, while others found self-hosting hard or laggy; those difficulty reports do not show the capability failing. Missing for 10: authentication on the OSS self-hosted server (users say it is open to anyone unless you buy Pro or put it behind a VPN), encryption enabled by default per one hands-on report, and consistent hands-on reports of a smooth setup.

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can self-host the rendezvous or relay infrastructure so session traffic stays on infrastructure I run

citations.quote: Server OSS: a free, open-source ID/rendezvous server (hbbs) and relay server (hbbr) that you can deploy on your own infrastructure.
Self-hosted ID/rendezvous and relay servers with Server OSS or Server Pro; clients connect peer to peer when they can and fall back to your relay.
You can use our rendezvous/relay server, [set up your own](https://rustdesk.com/server), or [write your own rendezvous/relay server]
Has used it for years with their own lookup/relay server and says it keeps getting better.
